WRS Raipur · Spring & Wagon QC · the inspector, on the tablet

Inspector walk — every screen, step by step

Before you start — five minutes, once

  1. On the shop PC, double‑click START.cmd; it prints the address for the tablet.
  2. On the tablet, turn mobile data off and join the shop Wi‑Fi.
  3. Install the certificate on the tablet once — server\certs\lan‑cert.crt, as in TABLET_TRUST.md — so the address opens with no warning and the camera and offline mode are allowed.
  4. Open the address START.cmd printed and accept Add to home screen.
  5. Sign in with the inspector account you were given.

Then go step by step. Each step shows the screen as it should look, the taps in order, what must be on your screen, and what to suspect when it is not. Tick Seen it only when you saw it.

The bench — springs

2.1 – 2.9

Sign in as an inspector. Everything here is one tap per spring.

2.1

The inspector's home screen

Seen it

Do

  1. Sign in with the inspector account you were given.
  2. Stay on the first screen — do not tap anything yet.

You must see

  • Two large cards under What are you working on today?: Springs and A wagon.
  • Under them, Your record today: how many springs, how many passed, the band tallies and the newest few with a time each.
  • A green Online dot and Nothing waiting to send.

What it proves

The first person to use this screen asked for two things: to see at once whether they are on springs or a wagon, and to see what they have logged. Both are here before a single tap.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:05 pm

  • the Springs card is on the home screen
  • the "A wagon" card is on the home screen
  • "Your record today" sits under the two cards

If it is not there

  • No Your record today box: the phone is not reaching the server — check the address and that the certificate was installed (section 1.4).
  • A red Offline dot: Wi‑Fi is off, or the phone has switched to mobile data — turn mobile data off.
2.2

The sorting bench

Seen it

Do

  1. Tap Sorting in the bar (or the Springs card, then Sort springs).

You must see

  • Bogie type CASNUB 22 NLB, Condition Used (6 bands), Spring position Outer.
  • The strip: six coloured buttons — Blue I 263–260 Green II 260–257 Yellow III 257–254 Orange IV 254–251 White V 251–248 Red VI 248–245 mm.
  • Below the strip a red Condemn this spring bar and the Gauge picker.

What it proves

These are the six bands of the shop's own G‑95 Rev‑II (Tables 28–33), not a five-band draft from the internet. The Roman numerals and heights should match the strip on the bench exactly.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:07 pm

  • a Bogie type chooser
  • Used / New
  • Outer / Inner / Snubber
  • six coloured band buttons for a used spring (6 found)
  • each button carries a height range: BLUE BAND I 263–260 mm | GREEN BAND II 260–257 mm | YELLOW BAND III 257–254 mm | ORANGE BAND IV 254–251 mm | WHITE BAND V 251–248 mm | RED BAND VI 248–245 mm

If it is not there

  • Three buttons, not six: Condition is on New — set it to Used.
  • No strip at all, a height box instead: Bogie type is on LWLH25 or LCCF20 (see 2.8).
2.3

Three springs by the band

Seen it

Do

  1. Tap Green, then Yellow, then Blue, a second apart.

You must see

  • This session: rises 1 → 2 → 3, Passed: 3, and Last: names the band just tapped.
  • A short chime on each tap.
  • In Your record today under the strip: the three new lines at the top, newest first — Blue, then Yellow, then Green — each with the time, ≈height, position, bogie and gauge.

What it proves

One tap per spring is the whole bench workflow. At 700 springs a shift nothing else is fast enough, and the record under the strip is how an inspector proves their own count at the end of the day.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:10 pm

  • session total went 0 → 3
  • Your record today lists the three newest first — 02:30 pm BLUE ≈261.5 mm · outer · 22 NLB / 02:30 pm YELLOW ≈255.5 mm · outer · 22 N / 02:30 pm GREEN ≈258.5 mm · outer · 22 NL
  • with a time against each

If it is not there

  • The count rises but the record does not change: the record box is fetched from the server after each tap — if the phone is offline it says so and fills in when the network returns (see 2.20).
2.4

Undo the last tap

Seen it

Do

  1. Tap ↩ Undo last spring (right, under the strip).

You must see

  • This session drops by one.
  • A line names what was taken back: Took back BLUE · Band I · 261.5 mm. 2 left in this session.
  • The line disappears from Your record today.

What it proves

A wrong tap is a certainty at bench speed, so the undo is one tap and says exactly what it undid. The record keeps a "taken back" mark internally — nothing is silently deleted.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:14 pm

  • total went 3 → 2
  • the undone spring is named: "↩ Took back BLUE · Band I · 261.5 mm. 2 left in this session. OK"

If it is not there

  • Undo last spring greyed out: the session is empty, or the last tap is still sending — wait a second.
2.5

Which gauge — and one with no calibration date

Seen it

Do

  1. Open the Gauge picker and read the list.
  2. Set Spring position to Snubber.
  3. Pick SSG‑02 in the gauge picker.

You must see

  • The gauges are named: ISG‑01, OSG‑01, OSG‑02, SSG‑02, each with what it measures.
  • On SSG‑02 an amber note: No calibration date is recorded for this gauge. Readings will be marked accordingly.

What it proves

Every reading carries the gauge it was made with, so a drifting gauge can be found later (the admin sees this on the gauge register). An uncalibrated gauge does not stop work — it marks the readings.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:16 pm

  • gauges named: ISG-01 — Inner spring gauge (N, OSG-01 — Outer spring gauge (N, OSG-02 — Outer spring gauge (N, SSG-02 — Snubber spring gauge
  • amber note: "No calibration date is recorded for this gauge. Readings will be marked accordingly."

If it is not there

  • No amber note on SSG‑02: the gauge register has a date for it — the admin can check under Gauges; the demo seed leaves it blank on purpose.
  • Set Spring position back to Outer before the next step.
2.6

Condemn a spring on sight

Seen it

Do

  1. Tap the red Condemn this spring bar.
  2. Read the panel, tap Back — nothing is recorded.
  3. Tap Condemn this spring again, then tap Crack.

You must see

  • The panel asks What did you see? with Off the strip (height), Crack, Corrosion, Deformation, Something else and Back.
  • An amber note says that for a crack, corrosion or deformation the photograph is the evidence — switch on photographing (2.7).
  • The tap on Crack records it: Condemned: 1, a low buzz, and in Your record today a red line — Condemned Crack · outer · 22 NLB · OSG‑01.
  • No question about re‑measuring — nothing was measured.

What it proves

The reason is the record. A spring condemned for a crack must never be filed as "200 mm" — the record shows the word, not an invented height.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:20 pm

  • reasons offered: "What did you see? For a crack, corrosion or deformation the photograph is the evidence. Switch on "Photograph springs while sorting" above —"
  • Cancel closes it without recording
  • the day's record shows it red, with the reason and no invented height: "02:30 pm Condemned Crack · outer · 22 NLB · OSG-01"
  • session total 2 → 3, condemned count up by one
  • no "re-measure?" question — nothing was measured

If it is not there

  • The record line shows a height instead of the reason, or a yellow Worth a second look panel appears asking you to re-measure: the phone is showing an old build — pull down to reload the page once.
2.7

Photographing while sorting

Seen it

Do

  1. Tick Photograph springs while sorting.
  2. Put a spring in front of the camera and tap its band.
  3. Put your hand in front of the lens and watch the badge.

You must see

  • The live camera opens directly under the tick box, large (not a thumbnail), with a green Photographing badge.
  • Each band tap saves a frame against the spring — no extra taps.
  • A hand in front → person excluded. It never says "spring 98 %".
  • Teach the camera (advanced) stays folded — it is not part of the day's work.

What it proves

The camera records evidence; it does not decide. The photograph is what a supervisor opens months later to see the crack that condemned the spring.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:26 pm

  • the live camera opens under the tick box
  • the picture is large (260 px tall)
  • a green "Photographing" badge
  • "Teach the camera (advanced)" is folded away

By hand: The spring and the hand are yours.

If it is not there

  • No camera, a grey box: the browser has no camera permission or the page is on plain http — the address must start with https:// and the certificate must be installed (section 1.4).
  • The camera opens somewhere else on the page: reload once.
2.8

A bogie with no band table

Seen it

Do

  1. Untick photographing.
  2. Set Bogie type to LWLH25 (BOXNS).
  3. Then set it back to CASNUB 22 NLB.

You must see

  • The six-button strip disappears; a single Free height — how many mm? box appears.
  • A note: No band table is published for this bogie — serviceable / condemn only. WMM 2.0 §309C.
  • The snubber position splits into Snubber outer / inner (G‑112 Table 26).

What it proves

Where the standard publishes no bands, the app refuses to invent them. LWLH25 springs are judged serviceable or condemned against §309C, by a typed height.

Checked on the build verified · 02:30:31 pm

  • the six-band strip is gone (0 band buttons)
  • a height is typed instead
  • the condemning height is cited to WMM §309C / G-112

If it is not there

  • A six-button strip on LWLH25: that would be an invented table — report it at once.

What it proves

The eight CASNUB categories from the WMM, item by item, with the standard each item cites.

If it is not there

2.13

Photographs and the blind pocket count

Seen it

Do

  1. Tap the Photos (4) tab.
  2. Read the four Pocket counts lines.
  3. Tap Recount on Bogie 2 · Side B and look at the counter, then close it.

You must see

  • Four frames: Bogie 1 · Side A/B, Bogie 2 · Side A/B.
  • Bogie 1 · Side A: 7⁄7⁄2 and 7⁄7⁄2 — agree.
  • Bogie 2 · Side B: Counted by Praveen Singh — a blind recount by someone else is needed, and no figures.
  • The counter never shows the expected number — you count what is in the photograph.

What it proves

A second person counts without seeing the first count. Only a supervisor sees "6 of 7 outer — one pocket may be empty". This is how a short bogie is caught before the exit gate, without anyone being led.

Checked on the build verified · 02:31:03 pm

  • four frames (4)
  • Bogie 1·A: "BOGIE 1 · SIDE A 7⁄7⁄2 and 7⁄7⁄2 — agree View"
  • Bogie 2·B: "BOGIE 2 · SIDE B Counted by Praveen Singh — a blind recount by someone else is needed Recount" — no figures
  • the counter does not show the expected number

If it is not there

  • The inspector's screen shows "6 of 7" or "short": that is a leak of the supervisor's view — report it.
  • The counter shows "expected 7": same — report it.
2.14

Parts in, parts out

Seen it

Do

  1. Tap the Parts tab.
  2. Read the balance line and open Show every entry.
  3. Look at the form: Came off · Went back on · Replaced with new · Scrapped · Not being refitted, then Category, Position, Part, How many.

You must see

  • The heading Parts in, parts out and a balance such as 40 off · 40 back on · 20 % of 41 expected positions covered.
  • In the list: the springs off at Dismantling, one outer spring Replaced with new — crack at the second coil, new from Stores, the rest back on at Reassembly. No warning box about a position with more back on than came off.
  • Recording a part asks which position; Scrapped and Not being refitted ask for a reason.

What it proves

Months after the wagon has gone, this list answers "was anything missing" — with the person and the time against each entry.

2.15

The air-brake test proforma

Seen it

Do

  1. Tap the Air‑brake test tab.
  2. Type 3.2 in row 1 Pressure in BP, watch the box, then clear it.

You must see

  • Single Wagon Test (air brake) — WMM 2.0 §720‑C — 14 rows: 12 readings with the specified range beside each, 2 yes/no rows (As specified / Not).
  • 3.2 against 4.9–5.1 turns the box red as you type.
  • The foot says how many rows are still blank; Record test refuses until every row is answered.

What it proves

The proforma the WMM requires after POH, with each limit beside the box so the person testing does not have to remember it.

2.17

A wheel, from the chalk on the disc

Seen it

Do

  1. Home → Switch wagon → All wagons → SER/BOXNHL/30914 → Continue checklist.
  2. On the Checklist tab scroll to the wheels (Axle 1 · bogie 1 … Axle 4 · bogie 2).
  3. Tap Axle 1 · Left. Type 917.

You must see

  • One large box: Tread diameter (mm) — the figure chalked on the disc.
  • Under it, as you type: below issue limit — Tread diameter 917 mm — last shop issue 919 mm, condemn 906 mm (WD‑97037‑S‑01 (WMM Ch.6, WD‑88089/S‑1)).
  • Flange figures are folded under Flange and tread figures, if the tyre defect gauge was used (optional).
  • Axle 3 already reads 917.5 / 917.8 in amber — this is the pair that blocks the wagon at the gate (section 3).

What it proves

The one number every wheel has is the chalked diameter; the rest is optional and stays out of the way. The limit and its drawing are quoted, never remembered.

The camera and the manual

Reading a painted number; asking the manual in its own words.

2.18

Reading a wagon number with the camera

Seen it

Do

  2. Point at any printed wagon number (a sheet of paper with SER/BOXNHL/30914 in large letters is enough).

What it proves

Eleven characters with gloves on, standing at the wagon, is exactly what a camera is for — but the person, not the camera, commits the number.

2.19

Ask the Manual

Seen it

Do

  1. Tap Manual in the bar.
  2. Search brake block condemning limit.
  3. Then search wheel diameter variation same axle bogie.

You must see

  • The first hit is labelled ANSWER — IN THE DOCUMENT'S OWN WORDS, large, with the page number, and a Source: line naming the manual and page.
  • More hits under ALSO IN.
  • The wheel question names IRCA Part III as its source.

What it proves

It quotes; it never paraphrases. 8,200 passages from the shipped manuals, on the phone, with no internet. If a passage does not exist it says so rather than inventing one.

No network, no permission, sign out

2.20 – 2.22

What must keep working and what must be refused.

2.20

Working with no network

Seen it

Do

  1. Turn the phone's Wi‑Fi off (mobile data is already off).
  2. On Sorting, tap three bands.
  3. Turn Wi‑Fi back on and wait up to a minute.

You must see

  • The three record with the usual chime; a banner: 3 springs are held on this tablet and will send themselves when the network is back. Nothing is lost.
  • With Wi‑Fi back the banner clears and Your record today gains exactly three lines — no duplicates.

What it proves

The shed has dead spots. Work continues; the record catches up; nothing doubles when the network flickers.

Checked on the build verified · 02:33:24 pm

  • three springs sort with no network
  • the queued count shows: "3 springs are held on this tablet and will send themselves when the network is back. Nothing is lost"
  • the queue empties once the network is back
  • exactly three more in the records (29 → 32), no duplicates

If it is not there

  • The page will not open with Wi‑Fi off: the app was never installed for offline use — that needs the certificate and one visit over https first (section 1.4).
  • Six lines instead of three: report it with the time — that would be a duplicate on resend, which the server is built to refuse.
